recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless a future work group decision reintroduces Consent.scope or changes Consent.category semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-15581 was a Published CBCC STU3 change request with Persuasive with Modification resolution asking that Consent.scope document why it was an isModifier element. The approved resolution added an IsModifierReason column and the text "Allows changes to codes based on scope selection".
initial_application: Git history shows the source spreadsheet gained a Modifier Reason column and populated Consent.scope with "Allows changes to codes based on scope selection" in commit 96e8cdaec5bd84db0bec8be6640ab1ce1d073fd4. The later explicit GF#15581 commit 7c8a912aeb6ff6bb22b167c37089bf18b5005a1c preserved the Consent.scope modifier-reason content while applying the resolved Consent tracker bundle.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini, but the current active Consent StructureDefinition no longer has Consent.scope. The later Published R5 issue FHIR-31903 eliminated Consent.scope, changed Consent.category to 0..*, and recorded the old element as merged into Consent.category in the cross-version map. FHIR-31903 also specifically questioned why scope was a modifier, so reintroducing an isModifierReason or modifier semantics for the removed element would contradict the later final decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source is correct for the current build because the original STU3/R4 element and its modifier reason were applied historically, and the current build intentionally removed that element.
